questions.question: Explain the difference between producers and consumers, and name three kinds of consumer with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Producers, like grass and trees, make their own food by photosynthesis. Consumers cannot make their own food and must eat other living things. Herbivores eat only plants, like zebra or impala. Carnivores eat only animals, like cheetahs or lions. Omnivores eat both plants and animals, like baboons, jackals and people.

questions.question: What is a food web, and what can happen if one animal is removed from it?
questions.expected_answer: A food web is many food chains in an ecosystem linked together, because animals eat many kinds of food and are eaten by many kinds of animals. Arrows point from the food to the eater. If one animal is removed, like the impala, the animals that eat it have less food and may eat other animals instead, and the plants it ate may grow more, so the whole web is affected.

questions.question: What are decomposers and why are they important?
questions.expected_answer: Decomposers are living things, mainly fungi and bacteria, that break down dead plants, dead animals and animal waste such as dung. They return nutrients to the soil, which plants take in through their roots to grow. Without them, dead material would pile up and the soil would run out of nutrients.
